title: WPMS/1313/2013 of Ravi Shankar Pandey Vs Uttarakhand Public Service Commision Haridwar AND ANOTHER

paras.text:
WPMS No. 1313 of 2013
Hon'ble Alok Singh, J.
Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Sr. Advocate with
Mr. Alok Mehra, Advocate for the petitioner.
Mr. B.D. Pande, Advocate for
respondent no. 1.
Mr. B.M. Pingal, Advocate for
respondent no. 2.
Undisputedly, petitioner was allotted a
residential accommodation no. G III/1,
Bhagirath Residential Campus, Haridwar vide
allotment order dated 06.03.2013. Petitioner
shifted his family and started residing therein.
Thereafter, vide impugned order dated
14.05.2013, allotment of the petitioner was
cancelled and accommodation, in question, was
allotted to respondent no. 2 Ms. Reena.
Undisputedly, no show cause notice was
ever issued to the petitioner before passing the
impugned order nor petitioner was afforded
opportunity of being heard as to why allotment
made in favour of the petitioner be not
cancelled on such and such ground.
Mr. B.D. Pande, learned counsel for the
respondent no. 1 and Mr. B.M. Pingal,
Advocate for respondent no. 2, tried to justify
that since respondent no. 2 belongs to reserved
category, therefore, she is entitled for
preference in the matter of allotment of
accommodation.
Mr. Manoj Tiwari, Sr. Advocate for the
petitioner, contends that legally there cannot be
any reservation in the matter of allotment of
residential accommodation.
I am not interested to examine this aspect
of the matter, at this stage.
In view of the fact that no show cause
notice was ever issued to the petitioner stating
the ground of cancellation of allotment nor
opportunity of being heard was afforded to the
petitioner as to why allotment order be not
cancelled, therefore, impugned order does not
sustain in the eyes of law. Present petition is

allowed. Impugned order is hereby quashed.
However, respondent no. 1 shall be at liberty, if
so advised, to issue show cause notice to the
petitioner stating ground of cancellation of
allotment giving at least four weeks time to
submit his explanation and thereafter, to pass
fresh order and decide the same by speaking
order in accordance with law. No order as to
costs.
 (Alok Singh, J.) 09.05.2014
SKS
